this paper provides a very good analysis of a current-source-fed induction motor drive system and presents a control strategy that is able to overcome many of the disadvantages of the existing systems.

, with the proposed control strategy, the current-source inductor motor drives have the same or better performance compared with the voltage-source approach, while having the additional advantage of reduced dc-link losses.

the current-source-inverter-fed motor drive system, when operated according to the proposed control strategy, is a very attractive solution in the low-to-medium power range, with the following advantages compared to the voltage source-inverter-fed drive system: 1) higher power density; 2) lower motor losses; and 3) lower inverter losses.

the proposed strategy provides a viable alternative to the voltage-source inverter approach for medium-power applications, where the current-source approach is traditionally used.
